content.title: Kevin Durant Injury: Ime Udoka reveals exact cause of Rockets star’s knee issue
content.text: According to Ime Udoka, Durant accidentally bumped knees with a teammate during Wednesday's practice, causing the brutal injury for the Rockets ahead of their first-round series against the Lakers. Kevin Durant has been officially ruled out by the Houston Rockets for their Game 1 matchup against the Los Angeles Lakers. Kevin Durant MIN: 36.41 PTS: 25.97 (61.02%) REB: 5.45 AS: 4.77 ST: 0.81 BL: 0.91 TO: 3.15 GM: 78 The superstar is dealing with a right knee contusion. Undoubtedly, this serves as a brutal and unforeseen gut blow for the Rockets to start their NBA Playoff campaign, putting the team's title chances in jeopardy. In his pregame speech on Saturday, Ime Udoka revealed that Durant sustained the injury after accidentally bumping knees with a teammate during Wednesday's practice. "Soreness. It’s very tender. It’s tough to bend certain ways. There’s not a lot of swelling, but he hit it in an awkward spot more than anything," Udoka told reporters. "It could be a regular bumped knee, and you can kind of play through that, but this is right above the knee, in the patella tendon area. It’s just very tender and sore. Like I said, pain tolerance is one thing, but the limited movement is more of an issue." Durant's latest injury is simply shocking after he had remained relatively healthy all season for Houston. He missed only four out of the team's 82 games while averaging 26.0 points in 52 percent shooting with 5.5 rebounds and 4.8 assists. With Durant out, the Rockets have no choice but to have all their hands on deck in dealing against the Lakers. "Hopefully, it's a one-game thing," Udoka said about Durant's injury.
